newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Sweden's Franzen sees lower debt yields - paper.
newsitem.headline: Sweden's Franzen sees lower debt yields - paper.

text.p: Sweden's economy is in such good shape that long debt yields should narrow toward levels in Austria, the Netherlands and Belgium, Swedish National Debt Office head Thomas Franzen told a Swedish daily.
"There is no reason to be satisfied with the current interest rate difference," Franzen was quoted as saying in the Wednesday edition of Svenska Dagbladet.
"In the long-term, it should narrow. With long-term politics, Sweden should not have higher interest rates than other countries."
The ambition to reach levels prevalent in neigbouring Nordic countries is not good enough, Franzen told the newspaper.
"The market has not fully discounted the development of state finances," Franzen was quoted as saying. "It deserves more attention and more credibility."
